name: County House Mountain
generated_description:
County House Mountain is a 1,142-foot summit in New Jersey. The County House Mountain Trail covers 1.6 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 184 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 40.83085, -74.94125 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 60 miles north of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Baldpate Mountain, Mount No More and Danville Mountain — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: It's rated Easy using the National Park Service difficulty formula (1.6 miles round trip, 184 ft of gain — about 100 ft of climbing per mile). The elevation profile on this page shows exactly where the steep sections fall.

faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 40.83085, -74.94125 in New Jersey. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.question: Are dogs allowed on the County House Mountain trail?
faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike County House Mountain?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is County House Mountain?
faqs.answer: County House Mountain stands at 1,142 feet (348 meters) in New Jersey.
